selected_evidence.requirement: node2 assigned to VLAN 10, node3 assigned to VLAN 20 over the shared link
selected_evidence.summary: nmcli created enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.2/24) on node2 and enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.2/24) on node3, both up

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 routes between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 (router-on-a-stick + firewall forward rules)
selected_evidence.summary: VyOS eth1 vif 10/20 sub-interfaces and firewall ipv4 forward filter accept rules committed and saved in /config/config.boot

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other across VLANs via node1
selected_evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping succeeded (ttl=63, one hop through router) after fixing the default-route asymmetry with subnet-specific static routes

selected_evidence.requirement: Traffic is actually 802.1Q-tagged as VLAN 10/20 on the shared link, not just IP-routed coincidentally
selected_evidence.summary: tcpdump -e on node1's eth1 shows ICMP traffic tagged 'vlan 10' from node2 and 'vlan 20' to/from node3, confirming real VLAN segmentation and inter-VLAN routing

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
